answer: Clone-key farms collapse when each new seat must occupy a unique map cell. The applicant records a vacant square on a public atlas, plants a serialized willow stake that must return a 7-second signed delay sample every 18 minutes, and posts a pearl bond of 19 POA plus 0.04 POA times the square of already-filled neighbors in that sector. Filing costs 0.31 POA. Auditors replay the stake traces against the beacon archive and confirm the cell is still exclusive. A reused square, a missed window, or two stakes sharing one serial seizes both bonds and freezes the sector for five epochs.
